subject: Tenor stack: conditional capacity tranches, co-term alignment, and auto-renew options
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Tenor stack proposal: tranches + co-term alignment

Hi Ravi / Sana —

Thanks again for the conversation today. Attached is a crisp proposal (Opentek_Term_Structure_v1.xlsx) that captures the structure we discussed. High-level summary: 

- Term: 3-year option (YR1 partial pro-rate + YR2–YR3 full) with the ability to convert to a 2-yr fixed in year 2 if desired.
- Tranches: Year-by-year committed token tranches (Tier A/B/C) that unlock additional burst capacity when usage thresholds are met.
- Conditional capacity: Canary window (30 days) in year 1 that allows short-term burst without breaking committed unit economics; incurs a capped overage rate.
- Co-terming: Option to align to Opentek fiscal year-end (co-term) with a single annual invoice; we can pro-rate YR1 to achieve alignment.
- Auto-renew: Default setting is opt-in auto-renew on anniversary; we can flip to opt-out per procurement/legal request.

Ask: please review the attached and confirm (1) rough agreement on the tranche sizes, (2) whether you want co-terming to run to your fiscal year (yes/no), and (3) whether procurement requires auto-renew to be off by default.

Next steps I propose:
- If OK, Marissa will prepare a mutual action plan and draft amendment for DocuSign.
- We’ll include the canary appendix in the SOW for clarity on burst windows and true-up cadence.

Attachments: Opentek_Term_Structure_v1.xlsx (spread with token tiers & pricing)

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick sync if useful.

Best,
Evelyn Hart

Evelyn —

Thanks for the deck. A few quick items from our side: 

- Co-terming: yes, we prefer everything co-termed to our FY-end (Jul 31). Pro-rate YR1 into the Jul 31 boundary if possible.
- Canary: we like a short canary but need clear SLA credit if the burst negatively impacts latency (we run customer-facing features during that window).
- Billing: procurement wants a single annual invoice and a single contract effective date; can you confirm how co-terming + pro-rate will look on Invoice 1?
- Discounts: looking for a structured discount tied to committed tranche thresholds.

Looping Legal so they can comment on the auto-renew default.

Subject: RE: Tenor stack proposal: tranches + co-term alignment — MAP + pricing math

Evelyn / team —

Per Ravi’s ask, I’ve drafted a quick mutual action plan and included a worksheet (attached) with the pro-rate example and discount ladder. Key points: 

- Example pro-rate: If effective date is Apr 10, 2028 and co-term to Jul 31, 2029, we would bill Apr 10–Jul 31 pro-rated for YR1 and then full annual invoice on Jul 31, 2029. See tab "Pro-rate Example."
- Discount ladder: 0–25% of committed => base price; 25–75% => 7% discount; >75% => 12% discount applied to committed token bucket only.
- Canary economics: 30-day canary with capped overage rate at 1.6x standard overage; any SLA hit during canary triggers a remediation credit (formula in appendix).
- Billing flow: single annual invoice at co-term date, with monthly usage true-ups submitted as a consolidated reconciliation at the co-term.

Action items assigned: 
1) Marissa: finalize MAP and attach draft amendment (draft-amendment-2028-03-23.docx).
2) Evelyn: confirm customer acceptance of the discount ladder.
3) Karthik / Camila: internal review of auto-renew and canary appendix language before sending to Legal.

Attachment: Opentek_Term_Structure_v1.xlsx (updated with pro-rate tab), draft-amendment-2028-03-23.docx

- Pro-rate examples: include a proration table for partial-year co-terms to make procurement sign-off easier.

Please incorporate and I’ll run with Legal for final language.
